**Pantone “Sky Blue”**

There isn’t a single universal “Sky Blue” in the Pantone system—different product lines (fashion/print vs. inks) have their own set of tones—but the most widely cited reference for a classic sky‑blue hue comes from the **Pantone® Fashion & Home Color Guide** and the **Pantone Color Bridge** books.

| Product line | Approximate Pantone # | Notes |
|--------------|----------------------|-------|
| **Fashion / Textile** | **Pantone 14‑4318** | Bright, slightly turquoise‑tinted sky blue. Often called *“Sky Blue”* in design briefs. |
| **Print / Ink** | **Pantone 15‑4320** | Lighter, more pastel version sometimes referred to as *“Soft Sky”*. |
| **General Reference** | **Pantone 13‑4205** | Very light, almost translucent “airy blue”; good fallback when only a general sky‑tone is requested. |

### How to choose the right one

1. **Check your source material**  
   - If you’re working with textiles or fashion fabrics, look up the color in the *Pantone Fashion & Home Color Guide* (the book will show the exact swatch).
   - For printing or digital work, consult the *Pantone Color Bridge* or the *Pantone Matching System (PMS)* catalog for inks.

2. **Match against a physical sample**  
   Even though the numeric value gives you a starting point, lighting conditions and substrate differences mean it’s always safest to compare the printed or woven swatch under the same lighting you’ll see the finished piece in.

3. **Ask the client or designer**  
   Many designers simply call out “sky blue,” so clarifying whether they meant a vibrant turquoise‑inflected tone or a very pale, almost white-blue helps avoid surprises.

---

#### Quick lookup tip

If you already know the Pantone number (e.g., 14‑4318) but don’t have the physical guide handy, you can quickly verify its appearance using online resources such as:

- [Pantone’s official website](https://www.pantone.com/)
- Free color conversion tools that map PMS numbers to RGB/HSL values (useful for screen previews).

Feel free to let me know if you’d like help converting a particular Pantone shade into web‑friendly hex/RGB values!
